lower-0862-s7-explain-with-models.description: Use a number line, a bar and pairs of counters to explain a short calculation.

sections.title: Where did you finish?
sections.label: Trace a move
sections.intro: Write the floor numbers in order, with 0 for the entrance. Each lift instruction tells you where to start the next move. To work backwards, undo the most recent move first.

blocks.html: Going up adds to the current level. Going down subtracts. To count the total distance, add the lengths of all moves.

figure.alt: A number line showing a move from −3 to 2 and then to −1.
figure.caption: The route has length 8. It finishes 2 levels above the start.

blocks.prompt:
A lift starts on level -9. It goes up 9 levels and then down 4 levels. Level 0 is the entrance.

Which level does the lift reach?
blocks.hint: Use the entrance as a landmark. From floor −9, nine floors up takes you to floor 0. Then take the final move.
blocks.solution:
A move up adds 9. After that move the lift is on level 0.

A move down subtracts 4. \(0-4=-4\)

\(-4\)

retry.feedback: The last move is down. Subtract its distance from the level reached after the first move.

blocks.html: The last level can be negative even when the distance travelled is positive. These numbers answer different questions.

blocks.title: Work backwards to the starting floor
blocks.prompt: A lift goes up 5 floors and then down 2 floors. It finishes on floor 1. On which floor did it start?
blocks.hint: Undo the descent first. After that, undo the climb.
blocks.solution: From floor 1, undo the descent to reach floor \(1+2=3\). Undo the climb to reach \(3-5=-2\).

retry.feedback: Floor 4 comes from applying the moves to the final floor. Reverse each move and start with the last one.

blocks.prompt:
A lift starts on level -2. It goes up 10 levels and then down 4 levels. Level 0 is the entrance.

Which level does the lift reach?
blocks.hint: Start on floor −2. Count how many of the ten upward steps take you to floor 0, then finish the upward move.
blocks.solution:
A move up adds 10. After that move the lift is on level 8.

A move down subtracts 4. \(8-4=4\)

\(4\)

retry.feedback: The last move is down. Subtract its distance from the level reached after the first move.

blocks.html: Show one calculation for the finishing level and another for the distance travelled.

sections.title: Which parts make the whole?
sections.label: Count the whole
sections.intro: A batch has a fixed mix. To work from just one colour, divide its count by that colour’s count per batch. This gives the number of whole batches you need for every colour.

blocks.html: A fraction compares some equal parts with all the equal parts. Another complete batch keeps that fraction the same.

figure.alt: A strip with two blue and three yellow blocks of equal size.
figure.caption: Count all five equal parts before finding the fraction that is blue.

blocks.prompt:
Each batch for a school event has 2 blue bands and 4 yellow bands. The organisers pack 36 bands using whole batches.

How many bands are blue?
blocks.hint: Combine the two colours to get 6 bands per batch. Find how many batches fit in 36 before counting blue.
blocks.solution:
Each batch has 6 bands. There are \(36\div 6=6\) batches.

There are 2 blue bands in each batch. Multiply by 6.

\(12\)

retry.feedback: You counted the yellow bands. Use the blue part of each batch.

blocks.html: Using the number of yellow parts as the denominator would compare blue to yellow, rather than blue to the whole.

blocks.title: Find the total from one colour
blocks.prompt: Each packet has 7 purple stickers and 3 white stickers. The packets use 15 white stickers altogether. How many stickers are in all the packets?
blocks.hint: There are 3 white stickers in one packet. Use the white stickers to count the packets.
blocks.solution: There are \(15\div3=5\) packets. Each packet has \(7+3=10\) stickers, so there are \(5\times10=50\) stickers in all.

retry.feedback: 35 is the number of purple stickers. Add the 15 white stickers to find the whole.

blocks.prompt:
Each batch for a school event has 3 blue bands and 5 yellow bands. The organisers pack 48 bands using whole batches.

How many bands are blue?
blocks.hint: There are 8 bands per batch. Use that to find the batch count, then use 3 blue bands per batch.
blocks.solution:
Each batch has 8 bands. There are \(48\div 8=6\) batches.

There are 3 blue bands in each batch. Multiply by 6.

\(18\)

retry.feedback: You counted the yellow bands. Use the blue part of each batch.

blocks.html: Draw the whole bar and count the parts before calculating.

sections.title: Will there always be a spare?
sections.label: Look for a spare
sections.intro: An even count can be grouped into pairs with no spare. One extra object changes whether there is a spare. Two extra objects form a new pair, so they leave the spare count the same.

blocks.html: A pair adds two. When an odd number of singles is added, the complete display still has one item left after pairing.

figure.alt: Three pairs of blue counters and one unpaired amber counter.
figure.caption: Making another pair leaves the single counter unpaired.

blocks.prompt:
A display has 8 pairs of books and 5 single books on a shelf.

How many books are in the display?
blocks.hint: Each of the eight pairs has two books. Count those books before adding the five single books.
blocks.solution:
There are two in each pair. Multiply 8 by 2, then add the 5 singles.

\(21\)

retry.feedback: A pair has two objects. Double the number of pairs first.

blocks.html: Several examples can suggest a rule. Explain what changing the number of pairs does to the spare item.

blocks.title: Complete the remaining pair
blocks.prompt: A tray has 6 pairs of badges and 3 single badges. At least one more badge must be added. What is the smallest number to add so that every badge can be paired?
blocks.hint: Pair two of the three single badges. How many singles are now left?
blocks.solution: The three singles make one new pair and one spare. Adding one badge makes a pair with the spare.

retry.feedback: Two new badges make another pair on their own. They leave the original spare.

blocks.prompt:
A display has 9 pairs of books and 5 single books on a shelf.

How many books are in the display?
blocks.hint: Nine pairs account for eighteen books. Include each single book once.
blocks.solution:
There are two in each pair. Multiply 9 by 2, then add the 5 singles.

\(23\)

retry.feedback: A pair has two objects. Double the number of pairs first.

blocks.html: A reason about any number of pairs earns more than a list of separate examples.

examples.title: A route between floors
examples.question:
A lift starts on level -5. It goes up 7 levels and then down 3 levels. Level 0 is the entrance.

  1. Which level does the lift reach?

    [2]

  2. How many levels does the lift travel in total?

    [2]

  3. Describe one move that returns the lift to its starting level.

    [2]
solution: (a) A move up adds 7. After that move the lift is on level 2.
A move down subtracts 3. \(2-3=-1\)
(b) Both moves add to the distance travelled. Add the lengths 7 and 3.
(c) Compare the finishing level -1 with the starting level -5.
Go down 4 levels.

examples.title: Work backwards from the final floor
examples.question: A lift goes up 7 floors, then down 3 floors. It ends on floor 2. On which floor did it start? How many floors did it travel?
solution: Undo the last move by going up 3 from floor 2. That puts the lift on floor \(2+3=5\) before the descent.
Undo the first move by going down 7 from floor 5. It started on floor \(5-7=-2\).
For distance travelled, count both moves as lengths. The lift travelled \(7+3=10\) floors.

examples.title: Two colours, one batch
examples.question:
Each batch for a school event has 2 blue bands and 3 yellow bands. The organisers pack 20 bands using whole batches.

  1. How many bands are blue?

    [2]

  2. What fraction of the whole batch is blue? Give your answer in simplest form.

    [2]

  3. A volunteer packs 15 yellow bands. How many blue bands should go with them?

    [2]
solution: (a) Each batch has 5 bands. There are \(20\div 5=4\) batches.
There are 2 blue bands in each batch. Multiply by 4.
(b) Use 2 blue bands over 5 bands altogether, then simplify.
(c) Divide the yellow count by 3 to find the new number of batches. Each batch needs 2 blue bands.

examples.title: Find the total from one colour
examples.question: Each bracelet uses 3 red beads and 2 green beads. All 12 green beads are used in whole bracelets. Find the total number of beads used and the fraction that are red.
solution: Two green beads go into each bracelet, so \(12\div2=6\) bracelets can be made.
One bracelet uses \(3+2=5\) beads. Six bracelets use \(6\times5=30\) beads.
Three of the five beads in every bracelet are red. The fraction stays \(\frac35\) when all counts are multiplied by 6.

examples.title: Pairs and spares
examples.question:
A display has 11 pairs of books and 3 single books on a shelf.

  1. How many books are in the display?

    [2]

  2. The number of pairs changes but the number of singles stays the same. Explain why the total is always odd.

    [2]

  3. Another display of this kind has 37 items. How many pairs are there?

    [2]
solution: (a) There are two in each pair. Multiply 11 by 2, then add the 3 singles.
(b) Group all the items into twos. The singles also leave one unmatched object when put into twos.
Pairs make an even total. The fixed number of singles is odd, so the total is odd.
(c) Remove the 3 singles, then divide the rest by 2.

examples.title: Test which change removes a spare
examples.question: Twenty-three cards are grouped into pairs. Sam adds 4 cards and says there will be no spare. Test the claim. What is the smallest number of extra cards Sam could add to make complete pairs?
solution: Twenty-three cards make 11 pairs and one spare. The four new cards add two complete pairs.
There are now \(23+4=27\) cards. Thirteen pairs use 26 cards, so one is still spare.
Add 1 more card to pair with the spare. Then \(28\) cards make 14 pairs.

extraPractice.prompt:
A lift starts on level -5. It goes up 12 levels and then down 6 levels. Level 0 is the entrance.

Which level does the lift reach?
extraPractice.hint: Start five floors below zero. The upward move passes zero, then the downward move starts from that new floor.
extraPractice.solution:
A move up adds 12. After that move the lift is on level 7.

A move down subtracts 6. \(7-6=1\)

\(1\)

retry.feedback: The last move is down. Subtract its distance from the level reached after the first move.

extraPractice.prompt:
A lift starts on level -6. It goes up 12 levels and then down 6 levels. Level 0 is the entrance.

Which level does the lift reach?
extraPractice.hint: Use floor zero as a checkpoint. After reaching it, count how much of the upward move is still left.
extraPractice.solution:
A move up adds 12. After that move the lift is on level 6.

A move down subtracts 6. \(6-6=0\)

\(0\)

retry.feedback: The last move is down. Subtract its distance from the level reached after the first move.

extraPractice.prompt:
Each batch for a school event has 2 blue bands and 5 yellow bands. The organisers pack 49 bands using whole batches.

How many bands are blue?
extraPractice.hint: One batch has seven bands altogether. Find how many whole batches fit before counting two blue bands in each one.
extraPractice.solution:
Each batch has 7 bands. There are \(49\div 7=7\) batches.

There are 2 blue bands in each batch. Multiply by 7.

\(14\)

retry.feedback: You counted the yellow bands. Use the blue part of each batch.

extraPractice.prompt:
Each batch for a school event has 3 blue bands and 6 yellow bands. The organisers pack 63 bands using whole batches.

How many bands are blue?
extraPractice.hint: Add the six yellow and three blue bands in one batch. Use that batch size to split the 63 bands.
extraPractice.solution:
Each batch has 9 bands. There are \(63\div 9=7\) batches.

There are 3 blue bands in each batch. Multiply by 7.

\(21\)

retry.feedback: You counted the yellow bands. Use the blue part of each batch.

extraPractice.prompt:
A display has 5 pairs of books and 7 single books on a shelf.

How many books are in the display?
extraPractice.hint: Make five groups of two books before counting the seven loose books.
extraPractice.solution:
There are two in each pair. Multiply 5 by 2, then add the 7 singles.

\(17\)

retry.feedback: A pair has two objects. Double the number of pairs first.

extraPractice.prompt:
A display has 6 pairs of books and 7 single books on a shelf.

How many books are in the display?
extraPractice.hint: Count the books in the six pairs. Count the seven single books separately so that each book is counted once.
extraPractice.solution:
There are two in each pair. Multiply 6 by 2, then add the 7 singles.

\(19\)

retry.feedback: A pair has two objects. Double the number of pairs first.

revision.body:
Reverse a route

Start at the finish and undo the last move first. Add all move lengths to find the distance travelled.

Find a total from one part

Use one colour to find the number of batches. Multiply the total per batch by that number.

Pair the extras

An added pair leaves the spare count the same. One extra object changes whether there is a spare.

A lift route
